svg.text: The collection samples the scene's Fourier space on a POLAR grid; the 2-D FFT needs a uniform RECTANGULAR one.
PFA gets there in TWO interpolations, and the middle state is why there must be two.
1 POLAR (Doerry Fig 3)
2 TRAPEZOIDAL (Doerry Fig 5)
3 RECTANGULAR
k_r[i,n] = (2/c)(f0 + i dF) per pulse n
Each pulse is an arc at its own aspect angle;
i steps outward in range frequency. Neither
k_x nor k_y is uniform, so no FFT applies.
RADIAL interpolate so k_y(i',n) = k_y(i')
T_s i' = T_s i cos(theta_n)
k_y is now independent of azimuth index -- rows
are LINED UP. But k_x still carries an angular
increment, so the grid is a TRAPEZOID, not a
rectangle. Hence a second interpolation.
AZIMUTH interpolate so k_x(i',n') = k_x(n')
T_s i' d_n tan(theta_n) = d_n'
Uniform in BOTH axes: a separable 2-D FFT
applies, so the hardware runs two 1-D passes
with a transpose -- the corner-turn -- between.
